Banning encryption is laughably stupid. Every site with a login form would have to shut down, otherwise they risk being sued for deceiving you into disclosing sensitive personal data (ex: bank account details). International business would sooner ditch the UK than agree to this, national business would significantly slow down and new tech companies wouldn't do very well without encryption.. In short, our economy would drown. It's safe to say that a flat-out ban on encryption will not pass.

So the Government plan is:

  • Force companies to remember everything you've done (securely and safely, with a key)
  • Force companies to hand over the keys to the government.

Here's a glaringly obvious issue with this dipshit plan to stop terrorism: Terrorists aren't going to hand over the keys, so the only people that will have their data exposed to the government are law-abiding citizens. Let's not forget that advanced encryption methods will instantly destroy keys after using them, so it would be impossible to prosecute an actual terrorist if one was found.

BTW, to even ask a potential terrorist to give up their encryption keys, you need to have some idea that they are a terrorist in the first place. You don't have concrete proof (if you did, they would be in handcuffs by now) so all you would be able to do is guess based on the type of person they are. This means reading everything they searched on Google, seeing everything they bought of Amazon and who they are following on Twitter. You would have to profile them. You need to profile every UK citizen for this to work, since you have no idea who could be a terrorist. Obviously it's not feasible to review each person 1 by 1, so some advanced algorithms need to be run on all the data stored on every UK citizen.

Does it sound a lot like the mass surveillance that they are already doing? Right, because this is the government trying to make it even more powerful. It will do nothing to stop terrorism, it won't even help fight against it because it can't. What's it for then?

tl;dr These measures can only intrude on regular people, because they facilitate mass surveillance. Terrorists can bypass mass surveillance easily.
